title: Lifecycle Routing Policy Table
subtitle: Make the policy table the controller-owned authority for contract-bound inference-unit routing.

in: Controller-owned post-review route selection after worker/reviewer bootstrap.
Policy table rule coverage for side-effect gates, repair routing, worker continuation, terminal blockers, closure review, and post-flight.
Typed policy selection contracts written into output-input and dashboard graph artifacts.
Contract and E2E tests proving route priority and no hidden fallback behavior.
A standalone harness run that proves the integrated policy table path on a realistic small living doc.
out: Adding unrelated inference unit types unless required to avoid false fallback behavior.
Changing the semantic role of worker, reviewer, balance-scan, repair, commit-intent, PR-review, closure-review, continuation, or post-flight units.
Dashboard layout redesign beyond surfacing policy decision evidence clearly.

parentEpic.title: Epic: encode lifecycle routing as an explicit policy table

objective: Implement the lifecycle routing policy table as the single controller-owned authority for choosing the next contract-bound inference unit in the standalone living-doc harness. Given typed controller facts, reviewer verdict, run policy, side-effect gate state, allowed inference-unit registry, and current lifecycle evidence, the controller must select the next unit, terminal action, or blocker through explicit policy rules rather than scattered fallback logic, prompt text, or reviewer prose. The result must be proven by contract tests, dashboard-visible policy artifacts, and a standalone harness run showing that routing can proceed through commit, PR-review, repair/balance, closure, blocker, and post-flight paths without silently falling back to the wrong unit.
successCondition: The lifecycle controller cannot choose a post-review route unless the route comes from the explicit policy table or an explicit terminal policy result. Every selected next unit carries a typed policy contract with rule id, selected unit type, reason code, required input paths, status, and dashboard/handoff metadata. Fixtures prove all priority paths, including missing commit, blocked commit, missing PR-review, blocked PR-review, repair/balance, worker continuation, closure-review, post-flight, and no-valid-route blocker behavior. A standalone harness run over a realistic small living doc reaches closed or a traceable blocker with policy decisions visible in output-input artifacts, graph JSON, raw-log references, and the dashboard.

runState.nextObjectiveAction: No remaining objective work. The standalone lifecycle proof closed in two iterations with policy-selected worker continuation, closure-review, terminal closure, post-flight summary, and dashboard graph policy edges.

data.name: Post-review routing moved behind policy table
data.summary: buildPostReviewSelection no longer contains the old direct route branches for closed, user-stopped, true-block, repair, worker, and fallback cases. Those selections now come through scripts/living-doc-harness-routing-policy.mjs, including blocked commit, missing commit, missing PR-review, blocked PR-review, closure-review, closure-review denial, repair/balance, worker continuation, user stop, and no-valid-route blocker behavior. Selection contracts now carry policyRuleId, selectedUnitType, selectedBy, dashboardLabel, handoffInstruction, requiredInputPaths, expectedOutputSchema, status, and gate metadata. Dashboard graph artifacts expose policy selections on relevant nodes and contract handoff edges. Full contract tests, PR-review policy E2E, and standalone lifecycle proof pass.

data.name: All post-review routes are policy-owned
data.criterion: Every controller route after reviewer verdict is selected by the policy table or an explicit terminal policy result.
data.proofRequired: Source inspection and contract tests fail if worker, living-doc-balance-scan, closure-review, continuation-inference, post-flight, or terminal blocker selection is chosen outside policy.
data.acceptanceTest: Focused lifecycle and iteration fixtures cover each selected unit type and assert policyRuleId or terminal policy metadata.
data.repairEvidence: scripts/living-doc-harness-routing-policy.mjs now includes explicit rules for user stop, blocked commit, missing commit, blocked PR-review, missing PR-review, closure-review denial, closure-review after preconditions, hard terminal classifications, repair-skill chain blocks, repair/balance, worker continuation, and no-valid-route blocker. buildPostReviewSelection now materializes policy selections instead of direct route branches. node --test tests/contract/living-doc-harness-lifecycle-controller.spec.mjs and node --test tests/contract/living-doc-harness-iteration.spec.mjs passed on 2026-05-13T06:50:20.000Z.

data.name: Policy output is a full typed selection contract
data.criterion: The policy table returns a full typed selection contract, not only a unit id.
data.proofRequired: Output-input artifact contains policyRuleId, selectedUnitType, reasonCode, requiredInputPaths, status, dashboard label or role metadata, and handoff instruction data.
data.acceptanceTest: Contract fixture reads post-review selection and asserts the typed fields are present for every non-terminal route.
data.repairEvidence: Policy selections carry policyRuleId, unitId, selectedUnitType, role, selectedBy, reasonCode, dashboardLabel, handoffInstruction, requiredInputPaths, expectedOutputSchema, status, and relevant gate metadata. Closure-approved policy results preserve both the closure-review unit and terminalAction. Contract validation fallback also selects continuation-inference with policy metadata instead of silently falling back to worker.

data.name: Commit gates route by state
data.criterion: Missing commit evidence routes to commit-intent, and blocked commit evidence does not route back to commit-intent.
data.proofRequired: Regression fixtures for missing commit and blocked commit states, including issue #288.
data.acceptanceTest: Lifecycle controller spec proves missing commit selects commit-intent and blocked commit selects continuation-inference through blocked-commit-intent-gate-needs-continuation.
data.repairEvidence: Missing commit evidence selects commit-intent. Blocked commit evidence is ingested into commitGate and routes to continuation-inference through blocked-commit-intent-gate-needs-continuation. The source-derived closure fixture now asserts blocked commit does not reselect commit-intent.

data.name: PR-review policy gates route by state
data.criterion: Commit evidence plus required missing PR-review routes to pr-review, while blocked PR-review routes to continuation-inference or blocker according to policy.
data.proofRequired: Contract fixtures and dashboard graph state for missing, satisfied, disabled, and blocked PR-review policy modes.
data.acceptanceTest: Lifecycle controller and Playwright policy-routing tests assert selected unit type and policyRuleId for each PR-review mode.
data.repairEvidence: Required missing PR-review routes to pr-review, blocked PR-review routes to continuation-inference, and disabled PR policy closes without PR-review. node --test tests/contract/living-doc-harness-lifecycle-controller.spec.mjs and npx playwright test tests/e2e/harness-pr-review-policy-routing.spec.mjs passed.

data.name: Repair, balance, and worker priority is explicit
data.criterion: Repairable document imbalance routes to living-doc-balance-scan, while ordinary actionable source work routes to worker only when no higher-priority gate is pending.
data.proofRequired: Ordered policy tests prove side-effect and proof gates outrank repair/balance, and repair/balance outranks generic worker continuation when imbalance is detected.
data.acceptanceTest: Fixtures cover repairable imbalance, repairable source work, and mixed states where commit or PR gates must win.
data.repairEvidence: Repair mode with executeRepairSkills routes to living-doc-balance-scan; repair mode without executed repair units routes to worker; generic allowed continuation routes to worker only after higher-priority commit, PR-review, closure, and blocked-gate rules. Existing lifecycle and iteration specs pass after the branch removal.

data.name: Closure and post-flight are policy-owned
data.criterion: Closure-ready evidence routes to closure-review, and approved closure routes to post-flight-summary.
data.proofRequired: Lifecycle contract fixture shows closure-review selection with satisfied preconditions and post-flight unit invocation only after durable lifecycle-result closure.
data.acceptanceTest: Closed lifecycle fixture asserts closure-review and post-flight selection came from policy metadata and not ad hoc lifecycle code.
data.repairEvidence: Closed evidence routes to closure-review after preconditions, closure-review approval carries terminalAction closed while preserving the closure-review unit, and closure-review denial routes to continuation-inference. Existing lifecycle controller post-flight assertions pass.

data.name: No valid route creates an explicit blocker
data.criterion: No valid policy route produces an explicit blocker or process-defect artifact, never an implicit worker fallback.
data.proofRequired: Negative fixture with inconsistent facts and no legal selected unit writes blocker evidence with owning layer, reason code, required proof, and raw artifact paths.
data.acceptanceTest: Lifecycle controller spec asserts the no-valid-route policy result is continuation-required with no selected worker unit.
data.repairEvidence: The policy table now has no-valid-route-blocker as the catch-all terminal policy result when nextIterationAllowed is not true and no earlier terminal/user-stop rule applies. The lifecycle controller spec includes a negative unroutable-facts fixture proving this does not become an implicit worker fallback.

data.acceptanceTest: Graph fixture builds a lifecycle with multiple policy-selected units and asserts each handoff carries policy metadata.
data.repairEvidence: collectLifecycleGraph now summarizes post-review policy selection into graph metadata. Contract handoff edges and terminal nodes expose policyRuleId, selectedUnitType, selectedBy, reasonCode, dashboardLabel, handoffInstruction, requiredInputPaths, expectedOutputSchema, status, and contract validation. The inspector renders a Policy Selection section for selected cards and arrows. node --test tests/contract/living-doc-harness-dashboard-artifact-graph.spec.mjs passed on 2026-05-13T06:50:20.000Z.

mermaid.text:
flowchart LR
  Facts["Typed controller facts"] --> Policy["routing policy table"]
  Verdict["reviewer verdict"] --> Policy
  RunPolicy["run policy + allowed unit registry"] --> Policy
  SideEffects["commit / PR / blocked gate state"] --> Policy
  Policy --> Selection["typed selection contract"]
  Selection --> Unit["next inference unit / terminal / blocker"]
  Selection --> Dashboard["dashboard edge/card policy evidence"]

data.name: Route priority
data.claim: Higher-priority gates must win before generic repair or worker continuation.
data.validationQuestion: When multiple facts are true, does the policy choose the safest route instead of the easiest route?
